questions.stem: The nucleus of the nitrogen atom N (Z = 7) consists of 7 neutrons and 7 protons. Its real mass is 14.007515 amu. Calculate the theoretical mass of this nucleus (amu). (mp = 1.007277 amu, mn = 1.008665 amu)
(Nitrogen nucleus: theoretical mass 14.111594 amu, real mass 14.007515 amu.) Calculate the binding (cohesion) energy of this nucleus in J. (N = 6.023×10²³, c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
Calculate the atomic mass of natural nitrogen, given ¹⁴N has a mass of 14.007515 amu and an isotopic abundance of 99.635%, and ¹⁵N has a mass of 15.004863 amu and an abundance of 0.365%.

Natural silicon Si (Z = 14) is a mixture of three stable isotopes: ²⁸Si, ²⁹Si and ³⁰Si. The most abundant isotope has a natural abundance of 92.23%. The atomic molar mass of natural silicon is 28.085 g/mol.
Which is the most abundant silicon isotope?
(Natural silicon: ²⁸Si 92.23%, M = 28.085 g/mol.) Calculate the natural abundances x (²⁹Si) and y (³⁰Si) of the two other isotopes.
Rank these chemical species in order of stability: H₂, H₂⁺, He₂⁺, He₂.
questions.explanation: Bond orders: H₂ = 1, H₂⁺ = ½, He₂⁺ = ½ (more antibonding electrons), He₂ = 0 (does not exist).

questions.stem: Consider the molecules BF₃; CO₂; CH₄; C₂H₄ and C₂H₂. Give the hybridization states of the carbon and boron atoms (in the order of these molecules). (B: 5, F: 9, C: 12, H: 1)

Rank the following bonds in order of increasing polarization: Cl–Cl, H–F, C–H, H–N.

What volume of concentrated 96.0% H₂SO₄ (density 1.84 g/mL) must be taken to prepare one liter of 1.00 mol/L H₂SO₄ by dilution?
What are all the possible values of the azimuthal quantum number l when the principal quantum number n = 5?
A hydrogen atom in its ground state absorbs a photon of wavelength λ1 then emits a photon of wavelength λ2. On which level is the electron after this emission? λ1 = 97.28 nm and λ2 = 1879 nm.
questions.explanation: 97.28 nm excites 1 → 4; 1879 nm corresponds to 4 → 3, so the electron ends on n = 3.

questions.stem: Given the angles: in NH₃ one angle equals 107°; in H₂O the angle equals 105°. Explain this difference and give the (VSEPR) formulas of these molecules (NH₃, H₂O).
options: Presence of unpaired electrons; AX4; AX2
Presence of non-bonding pairs (lone pairs); AX3E1, AX2E2
Formation of a π bond; AX1E1, AE4
